title: [Suite autour de Teichmüller dont] Teichmülleries, 1981-1982 : notes manuscrites (1981-1983, s.d.), lettres (1981, s.d.).

deep.reconstruction:
This is item 5 of Grothendieck's notes on conversations with Deligne (30 May and 5 June, presumably 1981). The topic is the compactification of the modular stacks ('topos modulaires') M_{g,ν} and their 'structure at infinity'.

(i) Conjecture. The compactified stack \hat M_{g,ν}, i.e. the Deligne–Mumford–Knudsen stack \bar M_{g,ν}, should have trivial fundamental group for g≥2. Grothendieck adds a hesitant remark for g=1: the π_1 should be finite cyclic of order related to 12 (most likely 'dividing 12'). The 12 recalls the abelianization of SL_2(Z), which is Z/12. He then states that the 'part at infinity' M^∞_{g,ν} should likewise have π_1 = 1 ('idem').

(ii) Definition of \hat M_{g,ν} as a moduli stack. The objects are proper (projective?) flat finitely presented X/S with sections f_1,…,f_ν such that:
- the geometric fibres are connected and reduced, with only ordinary double points;
- the f_{is} are smooth points;
- Aut(X_s, f_{1s},…,f_{νs}) is finite.
The last condition is equivalent to every genus-0 component carrying at least three special points, counting both nodes and markings. This is exactly the DM/Knudsen notion of stable pointed curve.

(iii) Question. For ν=0, does the smooth locus X_s^{lisse} of a stable curve embed in its (generalized) Jacobian? Here the Jacobian is Pic^0, a semiabelian variety, i.e. an extension of an abelian variety by a torus. This is the question of injectivity of the Abel map for nodal curves.

(iv) Properness. Verifying the valuative criteria 'seems strange'. This is the stable reduction theorem, the non-formal input to properness.

(v) Dehn twists. The 'twist' generators of the Teichmüller modular group T_{g,ν} (the mapping class group) should be loops around the irreducible components of the boundary M^∞_{g,ν}. This is Picard–Lefschetz monodromy around a boundary divisor. Combined with the fact that the mapping class group is generated by Dehn twists (Dehn–Lickorish), it explains (i): adding the boundary divisors kills all generators of π_1^{orb}(M_{g,ν}).

The page serves the program of describing the profinite/Galois 'structure at infinity' of the moduli stacks. This leads into item 6 (π_1^∞ via the formal completion along the boundary, compatibility with Galois action) and later the Esquisse d'un programme (1984).
errors: The g=1 remark is shaky. With ν=0 there is no DM-stable genus-1 object (infinite automorphisms), so M_{1,0} is not a DM stack; presumably M_{1,1} is meant. The compactified stack \bar M_{1,1} has trivial orbifold π_1: SL_2(Z) modulo the normal closure of T is trivial, since T=1 forces S^3=S^2, hence S=1, which also kills −1=S^2. The order-12 cyclic group is the abelianization of the open M_{1,1}'s π_1, not the π_1 of the compactification.
'π_1(M^∞_{g,ν}) = 1' is stated without precise meaning: it could refer to the boundary divisor or to a deleted neighbourhood of infinity, and the two differ. As stated it is an unproved guess.

For the Jacobian question, an Abel map X^{lisse}→Pic needs a base point or must land in a Pic^1-type torsor. Multidegree issues arise at separating nodes, so 'contained in its Jacobian' needs refinement (cf. later work on Abel maps of nodal curves).

deep.surprise_reason: These are conversation notes recording standard facts and guesses about the DM compactification. Simple connectivity of \bar M_g and the identification of Dehn twists as loops around boundary divisors are well known; the g=1 guess is off. The only interest is historical: an early (1981) trace of the 'structure à l'infini' theme of the Esquisse, arising in dialogue with Deligne.
transcription_corrections: '(non singulier [?] ?)' should probably read '(projectifs ?)', placed over 'propres'.
'd'ordre pas divisible [?] 12' is more plausibly 'd'ordre fini divisant 12' (or similar), alluding to Z/12 = SL_2(Z)^{ab}.

'(ce qui signifie que les composantes irréductibles de genre 0 de X_s — au moins trois points marqués …)' should read '… de genre 0 de X_s ont au moins trois points marqués, soit par intersection avec d'autres comp. irréd., soit comme pts f_{is} …'.
The crossed-out phrase under the inserted 'X/S munis de sections' appears to be 'munis d'une famille …', not part of the final text.
